A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VisMem and contain complete, readable main papers and appendices. Their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable matching and comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, ablations, cross-domain and continual-learning experiments, and inference-efficiency measurements in Sections 4 and 9.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and reports MathVista results for the comparison methods and nine base models.

M1.justification: Sections 3 and 7 retain the same memory-operation tokens, query builder, short- and long-term memory formers, inference procedure and two-stage GRPO objectives.

E1.justification: Tables 1–2 replace Math-V evaluation with MathVista. Appendix 8.2 changes the corresponding coverage from competition mathematics to heterogeneous mathematical and visual tasks. The other eleven evaluation benchmarks remain, and Math-V remains in the continual-learning experiment in Table 8.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same sixteen comparators, including vanilla. Comparator membership in the subset, generalization, continual-learning and efficiency experiments is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Figure 8 narrows its stage-training dataset citations to the pairs already specified in Table 8; for example, Stage 1 drops MMStar and MMT citations, retaining BLINK and MuirBench. This corrects the reported protocol description without establishing an experimental rerun. Model sizes and training budgets are unchanged.

E4.justification: The memory-component and invocation ablations, sequence-length sensitivity tests, cross-domain and forgetting studies, and subtask analyses retain their questions and evidence. The benchmark substitution does not introduce a new analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Existing plotting and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Changes concentrate on one benchmark and dependent aggregates. For Qwen2.5-VL-7B, vanilla/VisMem Math-V scores of 23.8/46.9 are replaced by MathVista scores of 67.8/79.8; Table 1 overall averages change from 51.0/62.8 to 54.5/65.5. Table 2 similarly replaces this benchmark's results across nine backbones. These are different-dataset results, not same-setting improvements.

T1.justification: Equations 1–15 and the appendix mathematical formulations are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract's headline average improvement decreases from 11.8% to 11.0%. The introduction's contributions and conclusion's claims about dual memory, generalization, forgetting mitigation, compatibility and efficiency remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations of visual versus semantic memory, transfer, forgetting and efficiency are retained. No substantive limitation, failure condition or applicability boundary is added.

D1.justification: Appendix 8.3 explicitly identifies Mirage, GRIT and MINT-CoT as the three exceptions to shared training datasets; v1 presents them as examples. This clarifies the disclosure without establishing changed training. Hardware, Table 4 hyperparameters and promised code availability remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Lu et al.'s MathVista paper as reference 37 while retaining the Math-V reference. The related-work discussion and positioning of VisMem relative to earlier methods are otherwise unchanged.

P1.justification: Editing is limited to the benchmark description, baseline-training qualifications, capitalization and caption wording. Section order and the overall narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 replace their Math-V column labels with MathVista, and Figure 11 redraws the corresponding radar-chart results. Figure 8's caption is corrected, with limited text and reference reflow. The figure/table inventory and overall design are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 clarifies training exceptions, reconciles Figure 8 with Table 8, and makes Table 1's recalculated averages more internally consistent. However, Section 4.2 now claims a 14.4-point reasoning gain although 60.2 minus 46.6 is 13.6, and Appendix 9.4 retains obsolete maximum gains after Table 2 changes. The benchmark substitution alone establishes no quality improvement. These opposing reporting effects leave the net quality change uncertain.
